The mechanism

Turn a rounding condition into finite arithmetic

The useful change of viewpoint is to collect algebraic conjugates into a trace. An integer recurrence then records the quantities relevant to rounding, and a companion matrix organises their residues. The numerical-looking question becomes a finite arithmetic calculation.

What becomes elementary: Trace identities connect the original approximation problem to an exact recurrence and modular computation.

Follow the bridge from conjugates to the recurrence before using the modular calculation. The original challenge and the supplied verification materials remain linked with the study.

Explore further constructions. Edition dates, sources and reference chapters identify the scope of each study.

Their powers complete to the integer trace , with an error that decays exponentially. A companion matrix then turns the trace recurrence into finite modular arithmetic. An order calculation modulo and , followed by lifting to and , gives an explicit solution.

1 Introduction and strategy

The operation to simplify is rounding a very large real number. Seek an exact integer sequence that differs from only by terms tending to zero. Adding the powers of the other conjugates supplies such a sequence; a recurrence will then let us calculate it modulo .
